Where should investors bet as Ambani's Rs 30,213 crore issue opens By Akash Podishetti , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 21, 2026, 09:48:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Jio Platforms is eyeing a staggering valuation of Rs 10 lakh crore for its upcoming IPO, sparking heated debates among analysts on whether to pursue Jio or Reliance Industries shares. The IPO holds the potential for investors to capitalize on India's booming digital economy, focusing specifically on Jio's telecommunications prowess, while Reliance offers broader sector diversification. ETMarkets.com With Jio Platforms seeking a Rs 10 lakh crore valuation in its IPO , analysts are divided over whether investors would be better off subscribing to the issue or buying shares of parent Reliance Industries . While some see greater value in RIL , given the discount on its Jio holding and its other businesses, others favour the telecom company for direct exposure to India's growing digital economy. At the upper end of its IPO price band of Rs 1,119, Jio Platforms is valued at Rs 10.3 lakh crore. Reliance Industries, which holds 66.43% of Jio before the offering, is expected to retain about 64.5% after the issue, giving its stake a market value of Rs 6.64 lakh crore. For Jio IPO LIVE updates, click here The numbers have brought renewed attention to the valuation of Reliance Industries and whether investors could get Jio exposure at a more attractive price by buying shares of its parent company. Arpit Jain, Joint MD at Arihant Capital Markets , said that applying a standard 30% holding-company discount to Reliance's stake in Jio brings its attributable value down to about Rs 4.65 lakh crore. This means investors buying RIL shares are also gaining exposure to businesses such as Reliance Retail, oil-to-chemicals (O2C), new energy and media, which Jain believes could offer attractive value at current valuations. Live Events Reliance Retail generates annual EBITDA of around Rs 27,000 crore, while the O2C business contributes about Rs 80,000 crore. Its investments in renewable energy, green hydrogen and media could offer further long-term growth opportunities. "Reliance Industries may appeal to investors seeking a diversified investment with potential value-unlocking opportunities across businesses, while Jio Platforms may be more suitable for those looking for focused exposure to India's digital and technology growth story," Jain said. Why investors may prefer Jio IPO For investors looking to participate directly in India's telecom and digital services growth, Jio offers a more focused investment opportunity. The company has more than 53 crore subscribers and has emerged as the country's largest telecom operator. Its growth prospects are supported by rising data consumption, improving average revenue per user (ARPU), expanding home broadband penetration and opportunities in enterprise services and artificial intelligence. Zerodha Fund House has launched the Zerodha BSE Top 10 Banks ETF , an open-ended exchange-traded fund (ETF) that seeks to track the performance of the BSE Top 10 Banks Index , offering investors exposure to India's 10 largest banks through a single investment. The new fund offer (NFO) opened on October 12, 2026, and will close on October 26, 2026. Investors can subscribe to the NFO with a minimum investment of Rs 1,000 and in multiples of Rs 1,000 thereafter. The BSE Top 10 Banks Index comprises the largest banks in the BSE 500, selected on the basis of free-float market capitalisation. The index includes both private and public sector banks, with constituent weights reflecting their relative size, subject to applicable limits. According to Zerodha Fund House, India has 41 listed banks, and the 10 banks represented in the index account for approximately 89% of the free-float market value of the banking sector. The ETF allows investors to gain exposure to this basket without having to purchase each bank's shares individually. Banking sector's role in economic growth Live Events Banks play a key role in financing India's economic activity by providing credit to businesses and individuals. According to the fund house, bank lending to sectors such as agriculture and allied activities, industry, services and personal loans has grown year on year in recent years. The ETF is designed for investors who want to take a focused exposure to the banking sector as part of their investment portfolio. Since the scheme tracks a sector-specific index, its performance will depend on the performance of the underlying banking stocks and the broader banking industry. The fund house also noted that several major banks in the index are trading below their respective five-year average price-to-book value ratios. But analysts are divided over how much of that benefit will translate into gains for RIL shareholders, with some arguing that the much-awaited listing has already been factored into the stock's valuation. The debate comes as Jio Platforms prepares to launch its Rs 30,213 crore initial public offering on October 21, valuing the telecom and digital services company at about Rs 10.3 lakh crore at the upper end of its price band. For Reliance Industries, which currently owns about 66.4% of Jio Platforms, that valuation puts its stake at roughly Rs 6.8 lakh crore. The question is whether the stock market is assigning the parent company the full value of that holding. What is holding company discount? A holding company discount arises when a parent company's stock market valuation is lower than the combined estimated value of the businesses and investments it owns, after accounting for debt and other liabilities. Investors often apply such discounts because shareholders of the parent do not directly own or control its subsidiaries' assets. The discount can also reflect corporate complexity, taxes associated with selling investments, capital allocation concerns and uncertainty over when the value of subsidiaries will reach shareholders. Live Events In Reliance's case, investors are valuing a diversified group with interests spanning oil refining, petrochemicals, telecom, retail and new energy. Even if Jio commands a higher valuation after listing, that does not automatically mean RIL shares will rise by a corresponding amount. Prathamesh Kadival, Research Analyst at Bonanza, estimates that RIL shares currently reflect a 36% discount on its stake in Jio, compared with a more reasonable discount of around 25% after listing.
